Hi Lina —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a very small acceptance roadmap and an evaluation checklist to use for the pilot. The goal here is to make the 30–60 day close predictable for both teams: clear milestones, owners, and exit criteria.

Attached: 2 files (GSlides + checklist). Also live link to the deck below so you can comment directly.

Quick asks:
- Can you review the timeline and confirm the week you can start integration testing?
- Please flag any internal review steps (security, legal, procurement) we should include on the timeline.
- If helpful, we can add a one-page procurement checklist tailored to Opal.

High-level milestones (in the deck):
1) Kickoff + environment access (Week 0)
2) Integration & smoke tests (Weeks 1–2)
3) Performance validation (Week 3)
4) Acceptance & contract signature (Week 4)

Link: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1OpalDraftSlides

Attachments referenced: 2027-03-12_Opal_ACCEPTANCE_SLIDES_v1.gslides (GSlides stub), Opal_Eval_Checklist_v1.xlsx (Excel stub)

If you can get feedback by Tues 16 Mar we can lock the pilot window and schedule the 30min alignment call.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Diego —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clean deck. A few items from our side:

- Procurement will need a "vendor security review" step before environment access. Can you add a placeholder for SOC 2 and data handling docs?
- We prefer the performance validation to be Week 4, with a short buffer for remediation after integration (can we shift the acceptance to Week 6?).
- I’m looping procurement here; they’ll send a standard questionnaire but it helps if you can pre-populate the answers.

Also: who on your side will own the technical runbook for tests (so we can coordinate resource calendars)?

Thanks Lina — good points. Quick notes from our side:

- We can add a "Security & Procurement" milestone between Kickoff and Integration (I’ll slot it as Week 0.5). Diego, can you attach our SOC2 letter and the KMS summary to the drive folder?
- Technical runbook owner: Evelyn will own the test runbook and coordinate with Opal’s engineers. Evelyn — can you add a test-owner slide and a short checklist to the GSlides (acceptance criteria per API surface + latency SLO)?
- Proposed adjusted timeline (in deck): Integration Weeks 1–3, Performance validation Week 4, Remediation Week 5, Acceptance Week 6. This gives procurement and security time to complete their reviews.

- Evelyn to update slides and checklist (action: Evelyn, due Mon 15 Mar)
